summary: Block-based email editor (Mailchimp-style): palette, reorderable WYSIWYG canvas, settings panel, isolated preview, and HTML export compatible with email clients. Import it from @devcommunityit/ui/editor.
whenToUse: Composing newsletters, event invitations, or simple transactional messages directly in the product.
Saving the email as structured data (EmailDocument JSON) and generating the HTML on the client or server with renderEmailHtml.
Offering non-technical editors a limited set of blocks (blockTypes prop).
whenNotToUse: Web pages or articles: use RichTextEditor.
Templates with complex conditional logic, AMP, or hand-written HTML: use a dedicated template engine.
Sending emails: the component only produces HTML and text; sending is left to the backend.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or initial document. It is serializable JSON: save it as is.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Receives a new immutable document on every change (blocks, text, settings).

props.name: onExport
props.description: Shows the “Export HTML” button and receives the output of renderEmailHtml.

props.name: label / aria-label
props.description: Visible title or accessible name of the group. Default: the editor's localized label.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Hides block actions and disables the palette and fields: canvas, preview, and HTML copy remain available.

props.name: blockTypes
props.description: Blocks offered in the palette (and accepted via drag and drop).

props.name: mode / defaultMode / onModeChange
props.description: Edit or preview mode (sandboxed iframe with the same HTML as the export).

props.name: previewDevice / defaultPreviewDevice / onPreviewDeviceChange
props.description: Width of the canvas and preview: settings.width or 375px.

props.name: emailLang
props.description: lang attribute of the generated HTML; dir follows the LocaleProvider.

props.name: renderEmailHtml(doc, { lang, dir })
props.description: Complete HTML document: role="presentation" tables, inline styles, hidden preheader, media queries for mobile, MSO ghost tables for Outlook.

props.name: renderEmailText(doc)
props.description: Plain-text alternative (the text/plain part of the multipart message).

props.name: createEmailDocument / createEmailBlock
props.description: Create documents and blocks with default values and unique ids (crypto.randomUUID with fallback).

props.name: insert/update/remove/move/duplicateEmailBlock, updateEmailSettings
props.description: Return a new EmailDocument without modifying the original.

props.name: sanitizeEmailUrl / escapeEmailHtml
props.description: Allow only http(s), mailto, tel, and {{...}} merge tags; any other URL becomes “#”. Text and attributes are escaped.

inherits: None: the component composes the library's GridList, Toolbar, ToggleGroup, Tabs, TextField, NumberInput, Select, and ColorPicker.

keyboard.action: Move focus (and selection) between canvas blocks.
From the selected block, enters the action bar and the inline text editor.
On the canvas, deselects the block: the panel shows the email settings.

keyboard.keys: Invio sul maniglia di trascinamento, frecce, Invio
keyboard.action: Reorders the block with React Aria keyboard drag and drop (Esc cancels).
Bold, italic, underline in the inline editor.

accessibility: The canvas is a grid (role="grid") that exposes the name and position of each block to screen readers.
Additions, removals, moves, and HTML copies are announced in a polite live region.
Every drag action has a single-pointer alternative (move up/down buttons, WCAG 2.5.7).
The preview is a sandboxed iframe with no permissions and a title.
Images require alt text: it is a block field and ends up in the alt attribute.
responsive: Below 1200px: palette and settings move into tabs next to the canvas; the canvas scrolls horizontally if the email is wider.
The Desktop/Mobile switcher shows the email at settings.width or at 375px; the exported HTML stacks columns below 620px.
customization: UI built with semantic tokens (--dc-*), light/dark theme, and RTL via logical properties.
The email content uses the document colors (settings), because email clients require literal colors.
Fonts: pick a safe stack from emailFontStacks.
commonMistakes: Inserting arbitrary HTML into blocks: rich text is Tiptap JSON and the renderer only allows a closed list of nodes and marks.
Forgetting the unsubscribe link in the footer (use a merge tag such as {{unsubscribe_url}}).
Using images without alt text or with non-https URLs.
Expecting identical rendering in every client: always test with tools such as Litmus or Email on Acid.

limits: No VML button for Outlook: the button is a table cell with a padded link (renders correctly, with square corners in desktop Outlook).
Media queries are not supported by every client: the hybrid layout stays readable without them.
Dragging from the palette is pointer-only (HTML5); with the keyboard, blocks are added with Enter/Space.
No image uploads, template library, dedicated undo/redo, or email sending.
Social links are text links, without logos.
